newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICA SET TO ANNOUNCE TELKOM SHORTLIST--REPORT.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICA SET TO ANNOUNCE TELKOM SHORTLIST--REPORT.

text.p: A shortlist of potential equity partners for the South African state utility Telkom is expected to be announced by Posts and Telecommunications Minister Jay Naidoo this week, the Business Times reported.
Naidoo would identify a shortlist of three to four potential partners, it said, following cabinet's approval of his proposals at its meeting last Wednesday.
The minister told parliament last month that the government hoped to decide by March on an international consortium to take a 30 percent share of Telkom.
The long-awaited deal, which is expected to spearhead a government's privatisation drive, has however not yet been accepted by trade unions.
Telkom chairman Dikgang Moseneke said negotiations would continue with the unions on the role of a future equity partner and that labour's concerns would be addressed where possible.

"However, our plans as regards the equity partner are firm. We need the technology, management and funding such a partner can provide in order to achieve universal access to telephony," Moseneke said.

Naidoo has already identified potential partners as France Telecom , Germany's Deutsche Telkom, British Telecom, Stet Spa in Italy, a Dutch and Swedish consortium of KPN and Telia, Bell Atlantic Corp and South Western Bell Corp.

The South African government has undertaken to double the number of private telephones over the next five years from four million serving mainly white areas at present to eight million, with a much greater penetration in traditionally black areas.
